segment: As in src/analyses_v2.py. The awarding agency code as recorded x product or service code x fiscal year.
amount: AMT in src/analyses_v2.py, federal_action_obligation as a decimal.
vendor: VENDOR in src/analyses_v2.py. recipient_parent_uei, or recipient_uei when the parent is blank, or '(no ID)' when both are blank.
hhi: hhi() in src/analyses_v2.py, over the vendors with a positive net in the segment.
proposed_handling: As built by handled() in src/decision_evidence.py (variant V1 of src/eda/base_tables.py). Each reversal pair keeps its net on its first row and its second row is set to zero. The two US Mint rows, rows to MISCELLANEOUS FOREIGN AWARDEES and the vendor '(no ID)' are left out.
civilian: Every awarding agency code other than 097. A blank code counts as civilian.
main_example: Among awards (contract_award_unique_key) with at least one row in awarding agency 036, product code Q201, FY2025, the one with the largest net over all fiscal years (AMT over every row of the award, as recorded) among those with rows in at least 4 fiscal years.
trace_rows: Every row of the award in every present fiscal year of Layer A, sorted by action_date, then modification_number, then the transaction key. The running net is the cumulative AMT in that order. Integrity flags are every flag_id in data/integrity/row_flags/ for the row's transaction key, with its name from config/flag_catalog.csv, joined by semicolons.
handling_change: For each row, how the proposed handling treats it: the first row of a reversal pair carries the pair's net, the second is set to zero, the US Mint rows, placeholder rows and '(no ID)' rows are left out, and every other row is unchanged.
trace_by_year: One row per fiscal year with rows. Net as recorded and under the proposed handling. Each segment the award's rows land in, with the award's net there under the proposed handling, the award's share of the segment's net under the proposed handling and the segment's HHI under the proposed handling. A product code or vendor ID differs from the year before when the set of values differs from the previous fiscal year with rows.
spread: Each row's AMT spread evenly by day over its period of performance, from period_of_performance_start_date to period_of_performance_current_end_date, both days included, then summed by fiscal year (October to September). A row whose start or end date is blank or unreadable is missing. A row whose start is after its end, or with a year before 1990 or after 2040, is impossible. Missing and impossible rows are counted and left unspread.
umbrella: When the main example has parent_award_id_piid filled: every award in the extract with the same parent_award_id_piid and parent_award_agency_id, in all fiscal years, with its first and last fiscal year, vendor IDs, net, product codes and extent_competed_code values. The umbrella's own rows are the rows whose award_id_piid is the umbrella PIID with idv_type_code filled.
jv_flag_test: A row passes the flag test when any of sba_certified_8a_joint_venture, joint_venture_women_owned_small_business, joint_venture_economic_disadvantaged_women_owned_small_bus is 't' in Layer A, joined on contract_transaction_unique_key.
jv_name_test: A row passes the name test when the upper-cased recipient_name or recipient_parent_name matches (^|[^A-Z])(JOINT VENTURE|J\.? ?V\.?)($|[^A-Z]).
jv_rows: Joint venture rows are the rows kept under the proposed handling that pass either test. Their net is the money held by joint ventures. Shares are of the year's net under the proposed handling, all agencies or civilian.
jv_vendor: A vendor ID is a joint venture in a fiscal year when its net under the proposed handling is positive and the rows passing a test hold at least 50% of that net. This is applied to the flag test, the name test and either test separately, and 'both' means the flag and name tests both hold.
display_name_jv: A vendor ID's display name in a year follows the display_name rule of src/decision_evidence.py (recipient_parent_name when the parent ID and name are both filled, else recipient_name, taking the name with the largest net), applied here to every vendor ID with a positive net.
name_review: The 50 vendor IDs with the most net on rows that pass the name test, over all years, among vendor IDs with no row passing the flag test.
segment_top: A segment's top vendor is the vendor ID with the largest net in it under the proposed handling (ties broken by the ID). Reported: segments whose top vendor is a joint venture (either test) that year, and the share of the dollars in segments with HHI above 2,500 that sits in those segments.
jv_largest: The 30 vendor IDs with the most net over the years in which they are a joint venture (either test), with their agencies, top product codes and years.
jv_parent_ids: Joint venture rows whose recipient_parent_uei is filled and differs from recipient_uei, after trimming. Their parent names are listed, the 30 with the most such dollars.
jv_member_names: For each joint venture vendor ID and year, its display name is upper-cased, the venture words (the name test pattern) are replaced by a space, and a lone A left before them is dropped. The rest is split on '-', '/', '&', ',' and ' AND '. Each part is normalized with norm_name() of src/decision_evidence.py and kept when it has at least 3 letters. A part matches a non-venture vendor ID with $1,000,000 or more of net in the same year when the first two words of the part equal the first two words of that ID's normalized display name. A part of one word matches only an ID whose whole normalized display name is that word, since matching it to every name that starts with it (AMERICAN, GLOBAL) gave tens of thousands of false matches in a first run. Marked for a check by hand: a part of one word, or a part that matches more than one ID.
jv_same_segment: A joint venture and a matched member that both have a positive net in the same segment.
jv_merge: Each joint venture is merged into its matched member with the largest net that year, its net added to the member's within each segment, and HHI recomputed under the proposed handling. The share of dollars above 2,500 is reported for FY2024 and FY2025, all agencies and civilian, with every match merged and with only the matches not marked for a check by hand.
services: Civilian rows whose product code starts with an upper-case letter other than A. Codes starting with A are research and development and codes starting with a digit are products.
services_check: Civilian services net under the proposed handling must be within 0.1% of the report's $96.9 billion in FY2008 and $229.1 billion in FY2025.
services_growth: Growth is the FY2025 net minus the FY2008 net. A group's share of the growth is its growth divided by the growth of all civilian services.
services_top_codes: The 20 four-character codes with the most growth in civilian services. Label: the description with the most rows in FY2025 (FY2008 when absent). Main agency: the civilian agency with the largest FY2025 net in the code. HHI: the FY2025 HHI of the main agency's segment.
services_above_2500: The share of the growth in agency x code pairs whose FY2025 segment has HHI above 2,500: those pairs' FY2025 net minus their FY2008 net, divided by the growth of all civilian services.
it_markets: For civilian agencies, codes matching ^(D3|D[A-K]) form one market per agency and year, IT services, and codes matching ^(70|7[A-K]) form another, IT products. Every other code, and every Defense code, stays as recorded.
it_check: Every two-character group the rule catches in FY2020 and FY2021 must be an IT group: the description with the most rows in the group starts with IT AND TELECOM or INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY.
it_effect: The civilian share of dollars above 2,500 for FY2018 to FY2025, as recorded and with the IT markets merged, HHI recomputed over the merged vendor nets. The part of the FY2020 to FY2021 step the merge removes is 1 minus the merged step divided by the step as recorded.
stable_code: A four-character code with rows in every fiscal year FY2008 to FY2025, whose description (the one with the most rows that year, upper-cased, every character other than a letter, digit or space removed and runs of spaces collapsed) is the same in FY2011 and FY2012 and the same in FY2020 and FY2021, and whose government-wide net under the proposed handling in FY2012 and FY2021 is at least 50% of its net the year before.
stable_lines: Trend lines as in src/eda/lines.py on the shivram-eda branch, over all 18 years and stable codes only: one awarding agency x product code, scored in the years its segment has an HHI. Kept with 6 scored years and $10,000,000 of net over them. Rising when the mean HHI of the last 3 scored years is at least the cutoff above the mean of the first 3, falling in the mirror case. Shuffled 20 times with seed 20261012, one generator for all cutoffs, lines in agency and code order, as in that file. All agencies, as in the report. The same code run on all codes in FY2012 to FY2020 must give the report's 5,772 lines and its rising and falling shares.
stable_line_dollars: A line set's share of dollars: the net of its kept lines over their scored years, divided by the net of every scored segment in the same years.
stable_share: The civilian share of dollars above 2,500 on stable codes: the civilian net in stable-code segments with HHI above 2,500, divided by the civilian net on stable codes, each year.
code_hhi: For each product code and year, HHI over vendor nets summed across every agency (government-wide) and across civilian agencies only (civilian-wide), under the proposed handling.
levels: Each year: the civilian share of dollars in agency segments with HHI above 2,500, against the share of civilian dollars in codes whose civilian-wide HHI is above 2,500.
leaders: FY2025 civilian agency segments with HHI above 2,500 whose top vendor (largest net) holds 50% or more of the segment's net. Each is checked against the civilian-wide market for its code: whether the same vendor is the top vendor there, its civilian-wide share of net, and the civilian-wide HHI.
subaward_source: The Award Data Archive listing (POST https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/bulk_download/list_monthly_files/) for FY2025 contracts, and the bulk download (POST https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/bulk_download/awards/) with sub_award_types procurement and subaward action dates in FY2025, the request behind the Custom Award Data Download page. The zip is saved in .tmp/subawards/, outside data/, and reused when present.
subaward_limit: The run stops when the zip is larger than 2,000,000,000 bytes.
subaward_main: The main example's subawards are the rows whose prime_award_unique_key is its award key. Reported: their count and summed subaward_amount, and the 20 largest subrecipients (subawardee_uei, else the name) with their share of the subaward total and of the prime award's FY2025 net.
subaward_coverage: For context: subaward rows, prime awards and summed subaward_amount by the prime award's awarding agency.
timing_dates: A valid date is a text whose first 10 characters parse as YYYY-MM-DD with a year from 1990 to 2040 (DATE_RANGE from Part 1). Two dates are compared on those 10 characters, because period_of_performance_potential_end_date is published in some rows with a time of 00:00:00 added.
timing_base_row: The base row is a row with modification_number '0'. Every other row is a modification, whatever its action type. Rows are read as recorded in Part 8 unless a column says proposed handling, and the award tables take in every row of the award, 097 rows included.
timing_order: An award's rows are sorted as in trace_rows() of Part 1: action_date, then modification_number, then the transaction key, all as text. The previous row and the earliest row come from this order. An award's first row has no previous row and is never counted as differing from one.
timing_covered_span: A row's covered span runs from the later of its action date and its start date to its current end date, both days included. It is invalid when the action date, the start date or the current end date is invalid, or when the span would end before it starts.
timing_sample: The main example (PIID 36C24220C0072, agency 036), the Emerson award, then the 10 awards with a civilian row and the largest net as recorded, then 12 drawn with random.Random(20261012).sample from the remaining awards with a civilian row and net of at least $1,000,000, sorted by award key before the draw. All must have rows in at least 3 fiscal years and at least 5 rows.
timing_date_checks: Six cases over every civilian row, by fiscal year. A case needing two dates counts only rows where both are valid, other than the first case, which is the count of rows with either date blank or invalid. Each case gets its rows, its net as recorded and its share of the year's civilian rows and net.
timing_action_groups: Funding groups by action_type name. Option exercises: EXERCISE AN OPTION. Funding-only actions: FUNDING ONLY ACTION. Every other modification is 'other', a blank action type included. The names were read from the distinct values printed in step 1 over all years, and no other spelling of either name appears.
timing_funding: For each award with a civilian row and a positive net as recorded over all years, the net of its base rows, option exercises, funding-only actions and other modifications, each over the award's net, and the count of its rows with a positive amount. An award with no base row has a base share of zero and is also counted in its own column. An award belongs to the civilian agency with the largest civilian net in it, ties to the lower code. The top agencies are the 5 civilian agencies with the most civilian net as recorded over all years. Per-award detail is too large to keep with the tables and stays in .tmp/timing/awards/.
timing_award_span: One row per award. Work starts on the earliest valid start date and ends on the latest valid current end date among all its rows. The work length is the days between them, both days included. There is no span when either is missing or the start falls after the end. Net by fiscal year, peak year (largest net, ties to the earlier year) and peak share (peak year net over net in all years) use the proposed handling, and the positive net test uses the same net. starts_before_data marks work starting before 2007-10-01. p8_award_span.parquet in .tmp/ holds awards with a civilian row and a positive net. .tmp/timing/awards/ holds every award, because the report's lines include agency 097 and Part 9 needs the same span for those awards.
timing_bands: Span and work length bands share the edges 366, 731 and 1,826 days, so 'up to 1 year' is up to 366 days, '1 to 2 years' is 367 to 731, '2 to 5 years' is 732 to 1,826 and 'over 5 years' is more. A percent band includes its lower edge and excludes its upper edge. Peak share and base share bands are tested exactly, on the dollars.
timing_no_span: The share of civilian net over all years in awards with no usable span. 'no_row_with_both' is the stated test: no row of the award has both a valid start date and a valid current end date. 'no_award_span' is the test the span itself applies: the award has no valid start date, no valid end date, or an earliest start after its latest end. The run stops above 10% on any of the four figures (each test, as recorded and under the proposed handling).
paid_ahead_rows: Part 9 reads rows under the proposed handling, with amt_h as their amount, and leaves out the rows that handling leaves out.
paid_ahead_row_rule: A row with a positive amount pays ahead when its covered span is more than 548 days. Check: more than 731 days. Rows with an invalid span count as unknown, whatever their sign.
paid_ahead_award_rule: An award is front-loaded when its net under the proposed handling is positive, its work length is more than 548 days and its peak share is at least 80%. Every row of its peak year pays ahead, whatever its sign. Checks: more than 731 days with at least 80%, and more than 548 days with at least 67%. Rows of an award with no span count as unknown. Rows of an award with a span and a net of zero or below have no peak share, are never front-loaded, and are counted as not judged.
paid_ahead_all_agencies: The report's lines and the stable lines include agency 097, as in the report, so both rules are applied to all agencies with the same row and award tables. Part 8's span tables report awards with a civilian row only. Tables by year are civilian, and the jump summary gives all agencies and also civilian and 097 lines on their own.
paid_ahead_provisional: Money paid ahead in FY2023 or later is provisional. p9_paid_ahead_by_year marks those years, p9_jumps marks jumps whose higher year is in them, and p9_jump_summary counts those pairs and gives the shares without them.
jump_pairs: For each line, every pair of back-to-back fiscal years with both years scored. A jump is a change in HHI of at least 1,000 points either way, with 500 and 2,000 as checks. A calm pair is a change of under 250.
jump_mover: The vendor whose share changed most between the two years, either way. A share is the vendor's net over the summed net of the segment's vendors with a positive net, as hhi() computes it, and a vendor with no positive net has no share. Only a vendor with a share in at least one of the two years can be the mover, so its net in the higher year is always positive. Shares are compared exactly, in whole millionths of a dollar, and ties go to the lower vendor ID. The higher year is the year with the mover's larger share, and an exact tie, which happens only when the shares do not change, goes to the later year.
jump_timing_linked: A pair is timing-linked under a rule when the mover's rows in that segment and higher year that the rule flags sum to at least half of the mover's net there. The largest award is the one with the largest net among those flagged rows, ties to the lower key.
jump_weighted: The weighted share is the segment net of the higher year in timing-linked pairs over the segment net of the higher year in all the pairs of that group, with the segment net as score() gives it.
pooled_endpoints: For each line, each vendor's net over the line's first 3 scored years is summed and the total is scored once with hhi(), and the same for its last 3 scored years. A line is rising when the last pool scores at least the cutoff above the first, and falling in the mirror case. A pool in which no vendor has a positive total has no score, and its line is neither rising nor falling. The count of those lines is in the table.
pooled_shuffle: One random.Random(20261012) for each line set, used in the order rising_counts() uses it: for each cutoff, 20 rounds, and in each round every line in the order line_set() returns them. Each line's scored years are shuffled, then the first and last three shuffled years are pooled. The averaged method uses the same shuffled years through classify(), and its counts must equal rising_counts().
pooled_dollars: A line's dollars are its segment nets over its scored years. The dollar share of a result is the dollars of the lines with that result over the dollars of all lines in the set. Shuffled shares are the average over the rounds.
pooled_share: Inside each code era (FY2008 to FY2011, FY2012 to FY2020, FY2021 to FY2025), each civilian agency x code is pooled over 3 back-to-back fiscal years and labeled by the last. The share is the net of pools with a score above 2,500 over the net of all pools with that label. The first two years of each era have no pool and stay blank. The yearly share is share_above_2500_all_codes_pct in p5_stable_share_by_year.csv.
award_part: An award part is an award's rows in one awarding agency and one product code, under the proposed handling. Its net is the sum of those amounts over all years.
main_vendor: The vendor with the largest net on the award over all years under the proposed handling, ties to the lower vendor ID. Every award part counts under its award's main vendor, in the baseline and in every spread.
spread_baseline: Each award part's net stays in the fiscal years its rows fall in and counts under the main vendor.
spread_awards: Spans come from .tmp/timing/awards/, the Part 8 span of every award. SPAN_FILE holds the same span for awards with a civilian row and a positive net only, and the run stops if the two disagree. Every award is spread, because the report's lines include agency 097 and an award with a net of zero or below still has a span.
spread_method: A spread award part gives each fiscal year its net x the span's days in that year / the span's days, both days included, computed by fiscal-year overlap and kept to 6 decimals.
spread_s1: S1. Each award part is spread over its award's span when the span starts on or after 2007-10-01 and ends on or before 2025-09-30. Every other award part stays as recorded.
spread_s2: S2. As S1, but the span ends on the award's latest valid potential end date over all its rows, or on its latest valid current end date when no row has a valid potential end. The later window test uses this end. An end before the start means no span.
spread_s3: S3. Every award with a span is spread over its full span, whatever its dates. Money landing outside FY2008 to FY2025 drops out and is reported.
spread_s4: S4. As S1, but only awards that award_548_80 calls front-loaded are spread. A front-loaded award outside the S1 window stays as recorded, under its S1 reason.
spread_reasons: A part left as recorded has one reason, tested in this order: no span, started before the data, still running after FY2025, started before the data and still running, not front-loaded. The fourth reason exists so the columns add up, since an award can be both of the two before it.
spread_moved: For each spread award part and fiscal year, the spread amount minus the baseline amount. The money moved out of a year sums the falls, and the money moved into a year sums the rises. All money landing outside FY2008 to FY2025, positive and negative, is the money dropping out.
spread_multi_vendor: An award has more than one vendor ID when its rows under the proposed handling carry more than one VENDOR value.
spread_examples: The VA award with PIID 36C24220C0072, the Homeland Security award with PIID HSHQDC11C00083, the civilian award with the largest net that award_548_80 calls front-loaded, and, among the awards S1 spreads, the front-loaded award with the largest civilian net under the proposed handling. Ties go to the lower award key.
spread_averages: The abstract's averages are the mean of the yearly shares, as in docs/reviews/2026-10-24_report_v1/recomputed.csv.
spread_lines: The report's lines and the stable lines keep the agency, code and years they have under the proposed handling, and are rescored under each rule. A year the rule leaves unscored drops out of that line for that rule, and the count of such line-years is in p12_swings. A line left with fewer than 3 years is neither rising nor falling, as classify() gives.
spread_swings: The change is the absolute change in HHI between back-to-back fiscal years with both years scored under the rule. A jump is a change of 1,000 points or more.
spread_rising: classify() on each rule's scores, shuffled 20 times with random.Random(20261012), one generator for each line set and rule, in the order rising_counts() uses it, whose counts must be matched. A line's dollars are its segment nets under the rule over its scored years. The check rows rebuild the lines from S1's scores with line_set().
spread_share: The civilian share of dollars above 2,500 is the net of civilian segments scoring above 2,500 over the net of all civilian segments, each under the rule. Under S3 the money dropping out is in neither.
spread_largest: The 10 civilian segments with the most baseline net in each of FY2016 and FY2019, ties to the lower agency and code. A segment a rule leaves unscored has a blank HHI.
civilian_lines: The report's 5,772 lines from line_set(), with the same settings and order. The groups are taken after the lines are chosen: all is every line, civilian leaves out the lines on awarding agency 097 with a blank code counting as civilian, and defense keeps only the 097 lines. Civilian and defense add back to all.
civilian_ways: Four ways of counting, each through the code of its saved table. averaged and pooled come from pooled_lines() on the proposed handling. baseline and S1 come from rescore_lines() and rising_rows() on each rule's scores, so each line keeps its agency, code and years.
civilian_shuffle: One random.Random(20261012) for each group and way, 20 rounds, in the order rising_counts() uses it. All cutoffs are drawn in order even where the table keeps one, as the results at a cutoff depend on the draws before it. A group's shuffled shares come from its own draws, so they are not a slice of the all-agency draws, and only the observed counts add back exactly.
civilian_reproduce: The all group must equal p10_pooled_rising, p12_rising on every result at 500 points, to two decimals. Any difference stops the run before anything is written.
